auth.setupIntro: This install has no owner yet. You will be the owner and can invite other people afterwards.
auth.name: Your name
auth.orgNameHint: Your company or your own name. Products live inside it.
auth.inviteIntro: {inviter} invited you as {role}. You will see all products of {org}.
auth.wrongAccount: This invitation is for {email}, but you are signed in as {current}. Sign out and open the link again.
auth.invitationInvalid: This invitation does not exist, was used or expired. Ask for a new one.
auth.noOrgBody: Your account is not part of any organization. Ask an owner for an invitation.
auth.haveAccount: Already have an account? Sign in first.
auth.regionHint: Currency and time zone come from your browser. Money in other currencies keeps its original value and is shown converted. “Today” and the daily summary follow this time zone.

projects.name: Name
projects.emptyBody: Create the first one to start. Only the name.
projects.keysIntro: Use these when connecting SDKs. They identify the product and are safe to put in a browser.
projects.dangerBody: Deletes the product, its keys and all its data. This cannot be undone.
projects.emptyMember: Ask an admin to add the first product.

members.title: Members
members.intro: People who can open {org}. Every member sees every product of the organization.
members.name: Name
members.inviteIntroEmail: The invitation goes by email through “{channel}”. You can also copy the link from the list.
members.inviteIntroLink: There is no email channel yet, so Octadash makes a link for you to send. Add an email channel and invitations go out on their own.
members.inviteRoleHint: Admins set up products, channels and rules. Members see everything and can press “I’m on it”.
members.invitedCopy: Invitation created. Copy its link from Pending invitations and send it.
members.invitedFailed: Invitation created, but the email did not go out: {error}. Copy its link from Pending invitations.
members.removeBody: They lose access at once. Incidents they were on stay as they are. You can invite them again later.

roleInfo.owner: everything, including deleting the organization and the install settings. At least one per organization.
roleInfo.admin: sets up products, areas, channels and rules, and invites people.
roleInfo.member: sees everything and can press “I’m on it”. Cannot change settings.

mail.subject: {inviter} invited you to {org} on Octadash
mail.body:
{inviter} invited you to {org} on Octadash, where the team follows uptime, traffic and emergencies of its products.

Open this link to create your account and join:
{link}

The link works until {date}. If you did not expect this, ignore this email.

errors.checkFields: Check the fields and try again.
errors.invitationInvalid: This invitation is no longer valid.
errors.invalidUrl: Enter a full address, like https://example.com/health.
errors.typeName: Type the name exactly as it is to confirm.
errors.wrongPassword: The current password is not right.
errors.lastOwner: The organization needs at least one owner. Make someone else owner first.

uptime.name: Uptime
uptime.body: Whether the site and the API answer, how fast, and when the certificate expires.
uptime.how: Nothing to install: Octadash checks from outside.

traffic.name: Traffic
traffic.body: Who visits, where they come from and which pages they read.
traffic.how: One Octadash script on the site.

usage.name: Usage
usage.body: Sign-ups, logins, key actions, funnel and retention.
usage.how: The Octadash package in the browser and on the server.

errors.name: Errors
errors.body: Browser and server errors, grouped, with how many people each one hit and since when.
errors.how: The Octadash package for the browser and Node, or any Sentry SDK.

money.name: Money
money.body: Revenue, MRR, churn and refunds for this product, with contracted, paid and net kept apart.
money.how: Connects to Stripe, Asaas or Paddle. Nothing to install in the product.

costs.name: Costs
costs.body: What this product spends on AI and infrastructure, and how much of the revenue is left.
costs.how: AI through the Octadash package for Node or OpenTelemetry. Infra through the provider API or a typed amount.

logs.name: Logs
logs.body: What the server did at each moment, to investigate an error or an outage.

newProduct.title: New product
newProduct.intro: Just the name. Where it runs and how data gets in, you choose later, in each area.
newProduct.name: Product name
newProduct.firstIntro: A site, an app or a SaaS you run. The others you add later from the product picker, one by one.
newProduct.nextBody: The product page opens with one card per area: Uptime, Traffic, Usage, Errors, Money, Costs. You set up what you want, when you want. Uptime takes one minute: just the address.

productPage.example: Example · real data appears with the first event
productPage.status: {receiving, plural, =0 {Nothing receiving yet} one {# area receiving} other {# areas receiving}}{waiting, plural, =0 {} one {, # waiting for its first event} other {, # waiting for their first event}}{toSetUp, plural, =0 {} one {, # to set up} other {, # to set up}}.
productPage.areasHint: Each card opens its area filtered to {name}
productPage.monitors30: {count, plural, one {# monitor} other {# monitors}} · 30 days
productPage.certSoon: {count, plural, one {A certificate expires in # day} other {A certificate expires in # days}}

areaPage.soon: {area} arrives in an upcoming version of Octadash. When it does, this screen shows how to set it up for this product.
areaPage.soonAll: {area} arrives in an upcoming version of Octadash. When it does, this screen shows it for every product at once.
areaPage.soonGroup: {area} arrives in an upcoming version of Octadash. When it does, this screen shows it for the products of this group.

overview.subtitle: {count, plural, one {# product} other {# products}} · {period}, until {time}
overview.incomplete: Some numbers are missing because the events database did not answer. Uptime states and emergencies are up to date.

table.title: Products
table.footnote: “—” means the product doesn't use that area. Click a row to open the product.

timeline.title: What happened · {period}
timeline.nothing: Nothing happened in this period: no outage, no emergency.
timeline.quiet: The other {count, plural, one {product} other {# products}} had nothing in this period.
timeline.more: {count, plural, one {# more on the product page} other {# more on the product page}}

uptime.title: Uptime
uptime.intro: Octadash checks each address from outside, on its interval, and tells you when it stops answering.
uptime.deleteBody: The monitor stops and its history is no longer shown.
uptime.empty: No monitor yet. Start with the site address; add a /health endpoint and a heartbeat for cron jobs later.
uptime.name: Name
uptime.kindSiteHint: Opens the address like a visitor and expects a page.
uptime.kindHealthHint: Expects 2xx and an answer that is not HTML, so a framework's error page does not count as up.
uptime.kindHeartbeatHint: A cron job or backup calls an Octadash URL when it runs. Silence longer than the interval is an outage.
uptime.graceHint: Extra time before silence counts as an outage, for jobs that take a while.
uptime.wakeTitle: A page that queries the database wakes it on every check
uptime.wakeBody: Databases like Neon suspend after 5 minutes idle and bill while awake. A check every minute on a page that reads the database keeps it awake all day. Point the monitor at a /health endpoint that answers without a query, or check this page every 5 minutes or more.
uptime.healthTitle: A /health endpoint that never touches the database
uptime.healthBody: It answers as long as the process runs. Pick your stack and paste it:
uptime.pingHint: Call it at the end of the job. Example for cron:
uptime.sameServerBody: This address points to the server Octadash runs on. If the server goes down, Octadash goes down with it and nobody is told. Set up the outside watcher in the settings, or monitor this product from another server.

failure.notHealth: Answered with a page, not a health response

settings.generalKeywords: name currency time zone money delete
settings.productNote: A product’s keys, monitors and its own alert changes are on the product, under Product settings.

generalPage.title: Organization
generalPage.intro: The name everyone sees and the defaults for money and time.
generalPage.name: Organization name
generalPage.nameHint: Shown in the product picker, invitations and alert messages.
generalPage.regionInfo: Money areas show totals in the main currency. Each payment keeps its own currency and value; the total converts it at the rate of the day it happened. The time zone decides where each day starts in charts, in “today” and in the daily summary.
generalPage.currencyHint: Totals are shown in it. A payment in USD keeps its value and is converted at that day’s rate.
generalPage.timeZoneHint: Decides when “today” starts and when the daily summary goes out.
generalPage.dangerBody: Delete {name} with its {count, plural, one {# product} other {# products}}, sources, monitors and all their data. Members lose access. This cannot be undone; you will be asked to type the name.

groupsPage.title: Groups
groupsPage.intro: Saved sets of products, such as “Main”. Choosing a group in the picker shows only its products, in every area.
groupsPage.emptyBody: A group saves a set of products to look at together. Create one from the product picker, under New group.
groupsPage.howToCreate: New groups are created from the product picker at the top, under New group.

profilePage.title: Profile
profilePage.intro: Your name, your email and your password. Only you see this.
profilePage.name: Your name
profilePage.nameHint: Shown to the other members, in invitations and on who is on an emergency.
profilePage.emailHint: You sign in with it. It can’t be changed here yet.
profilePage.nextHint: At least 10 characters. Your other sessions are signed out.

organizationsPage.title: Organizations
organizationsPage.intro: The organizations you are part of in this install. Each has its own products, members, channels and settings.
organizationsPage.newBody: For another company or client, kept apart from this one. You will be its owner and can invite people to it.
organizationsPage.name: Name

channels.title: Alert channels
channels.intro: Where emergencies go. Octadash sends with your own accounts, so nothing passes through anyone else. Signals never send a message: they show in the panel and in the daily summary.
channels.emptyBody: Without a channel, an emergency shows only in the panel. Add at least one to know when a product goes down.
channels.dialogIntro: Passwords and tokens are stored encrypted and never come back to the browser.
channels.name: Name
channels.secretSaved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
channels.deleteBody: Rules that chose only this channel will send to every channel.

errors.name: Give the channel a name.
errors.checkFields: Check the fields and try again.

smtp.passwordInfo: The password of the mailbox that sends, not your personal one. Gmail and Outlook with two-step login need an app password: create it in the account’s security page and paste it here. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.

resend.fromHint: With a domain verified on Resend.

telegram.botTokenHint: Create the bot with @BotFather and paste its token here.
telegram.chatIdHint: Press “Find it for me”, or paste it. Groups start with -100.
telegram.threadIdHint: Only for groups with topics. Leave blank otherwise.
telegram.botTokenInfo: In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, pick a name and copy the token it answers. Then add the bot to the group that should get the alerts and send one message there.

webhook.secretHint: Optional, at least 16 characters. Signs the body with HMAC SHA-256 in the X-Octadash-Signature header.
webhook.secretInfo: With a secret, each message carries an HMAC SHA-256 of its body in the X-Octadash-Signature header. Your service computes it again with the same secret and drops anything that doesn’t match, so nobody else can post fake alerts to your URL.

channels.testEmailOk: {count, plural, one {Test email delivered to # address} other {Test email delivered to # addresses}}
channels.usedBy: {count, plural, =0 {no alert rule sends a message} one {used by # alert rule} other {used by # alert rules}}
channels.rulesInfo: A channel is where a message can go. Each alert rule picks its channels; a rule with none picked uses every channel. If a channel fails, the others still get the message and this page shows the failure. The message language is per channel, so a team in Brazil and one abroad each read their own.
channels.neverSent: Nothing sent yet. Send a test to check it.
channels.whatsapp: Through the official WhatsApp Cloud API or your own Evolution API. Not available yet.

find.pick: Pick the chat. Not listed? Send the bot a message there and try again.
find.noToken: Fill in the bot token first.
find.badToken: That doesn’t look like a bot token.
find.none: No chat wrote to this bot in the last 24 hours. Send it a message (in a group, mention it) and try again.

alerts.title: Alert rules
alerts.intro: What becomes an emergency, what is only a signal, and how long to wait. These are the organization’s rules; any product can change its own.
alerts.productIntro: By default this product follows the organization’s rules. Changes here apply to it only.

levelHint.emergency: Needs action now. Message to the channels and the red strip on every screen until resolved.
levelHint.signal: Out of normal. No message: highlighted in its area and in the daily summary.
levelHint.off: Neither tells nor highlights. The data is still recorded.

alerts.noChannels: No channels yet. Without one, the emergency shows only in the panel.

monitor_down.title: Site or API down
monitor_down.body: A site or /health monitor failed 3 checks in a row. If it comes back before the wait, nobody is told.
monitor_down.info: Octadash checks every minute. One failure can be the network; three in a row is the site. Then it waits the minutes you set and, if it is still down, tells the channels and opens the red strip. Use 0 for checkout or login, where every minute counts.

heartbeat_missed.title: Heartbeat missed
heartbeat_missed.body: A cron job, backup or worker did not check in within its interval plus grace.
heartbeat_missed.info: Each heartbeat has its own interval and grace. When both pass without a check-in, the job is late and this rule decides what happens.
heartbeat_missed.note: Grace is set on each heartbeat.

cert_expiring.title: Certificate expiring
cert_expiring.body: The HTTPS certificate of a monitor expires soon.
cert_expiring.info: Octadash reads the certificate on every check. Most certificates renew on their own about 30 days before they expire; if one is still old this close, the renewal failed.

alerts.changedOn: Changed on {count, plural, one {# product} other {# products}}:

errors.starts: Starts when Errors is set up on a product

errorSpike.title: Error spike
errorSpike.body: Errors per minute well above this product’s normal for the hour.

usage.starts: Starts when Product usage is set up

signupsDropped.title: Sign-ups dropped
signupsDropped.body: Sign-ups away from what this hour and weekday usually have.
signupsDropped.wait: Needs 4 weeks of data to learn what is normal.

alerts.moreAreas: Each area brings its own rules when it ships (Money: payments failing; Costs: spend above normal). They appear here already set, so nothing needs to be written from zero.

groups.newIntro: A group gathers products to see only them: the overview and every area show the group's products. A product can be in several groups.
groups.name: Name
groups.empty: No products in this group yet. Choose them in Edit group.
groups.settingsIntro: The group's name and the products it shows.
groups.deleteBody: Deletes the group only. Its products and their data stay.

watcher.title: Outside watcher
watcher.intro: If the Octadash server goes down, no alert goes out and nobody is told. The outside watcher fixes that: Octadash sends a signal every minute to an outside service, and that service tells you when the signals stop.
watcher.howIntro: About two minutes, on the free plan of Healthchecks.io.
watcher.step2: Create a check with a 1 minute period and a 5 minute grace time.
watcher.step3: Copy the check's ping URL (it starts with https://hc-ping.com/) and paste it below.
watcher.step4: On Healthchecks.io, choose where it tells you: email, Telegram or another channel. Use one that does not depend on this server.
watcher.urlSaved: A URL is already saved. Paste another to replace it.
watcher.waiting: Waiting for the first signal (up to 1 minute).
watcher.failing: The last signal failed: {error}. Healthchecks.io will tell you if it goes on.

errors.url: Paste the full ping URL, like https://hc-ping.com/....
errors.ping: Could not call this address ({reason}). Check the URL.

warning.missingTitle: Nobody is told if Octadash goes down.
warning.sharedTitle: {count, plural, one {One monitor runs} other {# monitors run}} on Octadash's own server, and nobody is told if it goes down.
warning.missingBody: Set up the outside watcher: an outside service that tells you when Octadash stops signalling.
warning.failingTitle: The signal to the outside watcher is failing.
warning.failingBody: Octadash cannot call the watcher's URL. If this goes on, the watcher will report Octadash as down.

area.title: Set up one area
area.text: Uptime is the fastest: paste the address and it starts checking.

alerts.title: Choose where alerts go
alerts.text: Email, Telegram or a webhook. Until then, alerts reach no one.

watcher.title: Set up the outside watcher
watcher.text: So someone hears when Octadash itself goes down.
